Nestled along the eastern edge of Hanoi’s historic Old Quarter, the Hanoi Ceramic Mosaic Mural, known locally as “Con Đường Gốm Sứ,” is a vibrant testament to Vietnam’s rich cultural heritage. Stretching for several kilometers along the Red River dyke, this unique public art installation was conceived during the Millennium Anniversary celebrations of Thang Long-Hanoi in 2010.

Many people enjoy leisurely strolls or bike rides along the dyke, taking photographs and learning about the historical significance of each section of the mural. The area is also a popular spot for cultural events and educational tours, making it an integral part of Hanoi’s cultural tourism circuit.
